---
title: "After you have your level"
description: "Model types, limited time, disagreements and recording your level."
---

Use this page in [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) and [Phase 2, design](../02-design/index.qmd). Get your level from the [Analytical Assurance Decision Tool](index.qmd) first.

## The eight types of analytical model

If your work is a model rather than a one-off analysis, place it in one of [NHSBSA's eight types](../09-resources/r15-scoring-the-assurance-level.qmd#the-eight-model-types): policy simulation, forecasting, financial evaluation, procurement and commercial evaluation, planning, science based, allocation of funds and conceptual.

The type is not scored. Use it to check your impact scores. If your model allocates funds and does not score highly on Decision and Finance, look again at those scores.

## When you disagree

If the commissioner and the analyst disagree on the level, the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead decides. See [where each disagreement goes](../06-roles/index.qmd#when-you-disagree).

## When time is short {#when-there-is-not-enough-time}

If you do not have enough time or resource for all the assurance your level needs:

1. Keep the level you scored, and record that level.
2. Do the Level 1 checks. Add the other checks of your level as time allows. This is the Analytical Assurance Decision Tool's rule for working at pace.
3. Reduce the scope of the question, not the assurance applied to the answer.
4. Complete the highest-risk checks first.
5. State in the output, and in the [quality assurance statement](/guidance/09-resources/r5-quality-assurance-statement.qmd), which assurance you did not do and what that means for how the analysis can be used.
6. Tell the commissioner how you addressed the risks, what risks remain and the caveats that go with them.

## If the playbook and the Analytical Assurance Decision Tool differ

If a scale or the matrix in this playbook differs from the Analytical Assurance Decision Tool, follow the tool. Report the difference through [Who to ask](/guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd).

## Record your level in the Specification

Record the level, the date and who agreed it in the Specification. Attach the completed tool to the quality assurance plan, as its template asks. At Level 1 there is no separate assurance plan, so attach it to the Specification. The analyst writes the Specification and shares it with the commissioner for sign off. See [what to record at scoping and at design](index.qmd#outputs-of-setting-your-level).

| Level | Who agrees the level |
|---|---|
| **Level 1 Standard** | You score the level and record it yourself |
| **Level 2 Enhanced** | You and the commissioner agree it together |
| **Level 3 Comprehensive** | The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead confirms it |
| **Level 4 BCA** | The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead confirms it |

: Who agrees the assurance level, by level
